text: Boolos's 'ontological innocence' thesis about plural quantification claims that:
choices: plural quantification commits us to no objects beyond the individuals already in the range of the singular quantifiers
pluralities are a new kind of abstract object, merely cheaper than sets
every plurality is identical to the set of its members
plural logic quantifies over properties rather than objects
explanation: Innocence says the values of a plural variable are just individuals taken several at a time, so ∃xx adds no new object — no set, class, or plurality-as-entity — to the ontology. Each distractor smuggles in a new entity (a plurality-object, a set, or a property), which is exactly what the thesis denies.
